notes: Perfect claim overlap (C7, C96, C117) regarding TPI fitness findings. Both agree that TPI-producing plants were not fitter than TPI-silenced plants in nature, representing a valid negative result.

High overlap (C8, C118, C119, C120) on TPI behavioral assays. LLM finds the evidence well-supported, but peer reviewers suggest these experiments 'could be omitted' and may 'distract from the rest of the work,' indicating uncertainty about their contribution to the manuscript.

Strong overlap (C5, C6, C91, C110, C111, C113, C115) on the core HIPV fitness findings. Both strongly agree that GLV-emitting plants had higher predation rates and increased fitness (buds/flowers) when predators were present. Peer reviewers commend this as 'a big step toward providing an answer' to the central question.

Moderate overlap (C122, C123) on the inactive irPI construct in hemi-irLOX2 plants. LLM finds the explanation well-reasoned and supported. Peer reviewers express concern about insufficient justification for focusing on hemizygous lines and request better explanation of VOC effects comparison.

Overlap on fitness proxy justification (C127, C128, C131, C132). LLM finds bud/flower counts well-justified as fitness proxies. Peer reviewers express regret that true seed production couldn't be measured due to GMO regulations, introducing uncertainty about whether the proxy fully captures Darwinian fitness.

Partial overlap (C48, C49, C52, C53) on experimental design and fitness metrics. LLM supports the overall design appropriateness. Peer review uncertainty focuses specifically on the fitness measurement limitation (inability to measure seeds), which is a subset of the broader design claims.

Minimal overlap (C68) on GLV chemical modification by herbivore oral secretions. LLM accepts the claim as supported. Peer reviewers identify a technical error, stating the process is a 'rearrangement, not an isomerisation' and require correction of the chemical description.

Minimal overlap (C104) but both agree. LLM supports the 2010 control experiment showing fitness differences depend on predator presence. Peer reviewers affirm the overall experimental logic including controls, implicitly supporting this claim.

Minimal overlap (C94) on differential predation rates. Both support that GLVs function as short-range cues. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm that plants emitting less VOCs attract fewer predators, consistent with LLM's assessment.
